facts.F1: Story #6361 S03c Package Forecasting, nwdes feature A of three (rules first). Before any Forecasting type moves into Modules/Forecasting, make the module rules shared and make every architecture rule that names Forecasting's namespaces, folders or files also see Modules/Forecasting, and add a safety net that shows forecasts and forecast answers do not change. Behaviour-free: routes, DTOs, responses and forecast results stay the same. Design: docs/feature/story-6361-s03c-package-forecasting/feature-delta.md (slices A1-A3, Ratchet design).

facts.F17: Shared rules owner: FlowMetricsModuleRules is renamed to ModuleRules (Architecture/ModuleRules.cs), module namespaces stay parameters. The two private Application shapes move into it: ApplicationIsReachedFromOutsideOnlyBy (from FlowMetricsInboundApplicationArchUnitTest, returns InboundVerdict) and OutboundEdges with the OutboundVerdict record (from FlowMetricsApplicationOutboundArchUnitTest, made internal). Flow metrics tests call the lifted methods with their own constants; their made-up-offender tests keep their meaning. Rename is a move-only commit, the lift an edit commit. No second rules class.
facts.F18: Made-up types that prove a widened Forecasting pattern live in the test assembly under namespaces the real widened pattern matches, i.e. below Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.Forecasting, with a last segment naming them as fixtures (for example Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.Forecasting.Adapters.Background.ForecastingFixtures). Deviation from the example namespace Lighthouse.Backend.Modules.ForecastingFixtures in the story design: the widened patterns end in (\.|$), so a type in Modules.ForecastingFixtures lies outside them and would prove only a rule shape with a substituted pattern, not the real constant. Rule-shape cases that pass their namespaces as parameters may keep the Modules.ForecastingFixtures namespaces the S02 way.
facts.F19: Widening per rule (Ratchet design, Rules first): ModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest.ForecastingPattern gains |^Lighthouse\.Backend\.Modules\.Forecasting(\.|$) and Flow metrics outbound rule keeps reading it; SimulatedRunIsolationArchUnitTest uses an old-or-module namespace pattern; RealityCheckReadOnlyArchUnitTest matches the two policies by typeof and forbids ApplicationCoreRules.ApplicationCore minus the two policies; DependencyAwareForecastSeamArchUnitTest subject is the update components or Modules.Forecasting.Adapters.Background, exemption by typeof(ForecastUpdater); FastWithManyFeaturesArchUnitTest locates ForecastService.cs and ForecastUpdater.cs by file name under the production source as it does for ForecastLane.cs; RefinementModuleArchUnitTest forbidden background set adds Modules.Forecasting.Adapters. UpdateHoldsAreForecastOnly, ForecastFilterSeam and DomainEventHandlerOrderPin already key on typeof or short names and are left unchanged. RecurringBlackoutEventsSeam and StalenessPolicyPurity: the crafter checks whether a Forecasting type is in their subject or target set and widens to ApplicationCore only if so. Flow metrics full-name strings for Forecasting types are not touched here (feature B rewrites them).

facts.F20: Safety net: a port-level seeded check under Tests/Acceptance/Forecasting runs ForecastSimulation and ForecastService (How Many and When) with DrawsFromAPinnedStartingNumber over ServicePortHarness and compares percentiles to literal values written in the test. A new Scripts/examine/bin/forecast-answers-compare, built like metrics-answers-compare (usage: forecast-answers-compare [base-revision [candidate-revision]]), captures the bodies of the GET forecast endpoints on seeded demo data with a fixed seed and diffs them; declared in .nwave/examine.json. The production-like database comparison is a maintainer-run step, not an EXAMINE expectation.
facts.F21: Formal verification: no checker selected. No state, transition, protocol, concurrency or recovery behaviour changes. Rule claims are finite and decided exactly by the compiled IL with a made-up offender per rule as falsifier; the forecast-preservation claim compares code with itself, so a pinned seed with literal expected percentiles is the honest falsifier. Quint, TLA+/TLC and Agda would model nothing; no model written, no checker run or claimed. Liveness not applicable: synchronous rule evaluation and a one-shot capture have no progress property. Property-based testing not applicable: every law is a finite enumeration of rules, made-up types and named endpoints.
facts.F22: Carriers, all test-side: rule verdicts are KernelRuleVerdict, InboundVerdict and OutboundVerdict owned by ModuleRules and KernelRules (Architecture folder); dependency facts are IlDependent from IlDependencies; per-fixture state is the lazily read Mono.Cecil ModuleDefinition disposed at one-time teardown; the seeded check holds ServicePortHarness per scenario; the compare script holds captured bodies in a temp directory. Layers: application rules only; no adapter, infrastructure or recovery layer changes.
facts.F23: One oracle file per slice; a later slice never edits an earlier slice oracle or support files. No nWave scenario tags in code. Arch rule tests assert the rule failure names the offender, not counts. Comments carry no internal ids.
